clue.text: Now, on date to be taken for a ride, where are you? If you have not done so already, enter as per fill at 1 Across, with alternate letters filling white squares

definitions.note: a question; the answer replies with your location in this very grid

indicators.text: to be taken for a ride
indicators.note: being taken for a ride means being tricked or led astray, so the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stood up on a date, asked where they are, followed by instructions for filling the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the letters of NOW ON DATE. The reply to 'where are you?' is your position while solving: at this very entry. The rest of the clue is the puzzle's instruction for the unclued 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: Solving this clue you are literally positioned at the light numbered one in the down direction, a self-referential joke.

clue.text: In Japan, the only circular temple

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of words that follows, crossing their boundaries

explanation.surface: A claim that Japan has just one round shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Japan' reads as a location, but 'In' is the signal that the letters lie inside JAPAN THE ONLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is the famous domed, round-plan ancient Roman temple to all the gods.

clue.text: Earldoms? Do not present incorrectly as provinces

indicators.note: Do is to be absent from the letters, so those two letters are taken out of the pool
presenting something incorrectly means putting it in the wrong order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning not to misrepresent earldoms as mere provinces.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D and O from EARLDOMS, leaving EARLMS, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms or territories, so they can stand for provinces or domains under a ruler.

clue.text: I make an offer in the same place

parts.note: to bid is to make an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone making an offer for something at the same spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibid is the Latin abbreviation used in footnotes meaning the reference is from the work just cited.

clue.text: See 25
Rib principally toughens the thorax, reportedly? Enter as per fill at 1 Across, with alternate letters filling white squares

definitions.note: a verb: to make fun of someone

indicators.note: said aloud, three of that one letter sounds like a word meaning rib

parts.note: the principal, leading, letters of toughens, the and thorax are three Ts, said as 'tees'

explanation.surface: A claim that a rib strengthens the chest, followed by the puzzle's grid-filling instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: The three first letters are T, T, T: said aloud, 'tees' sounds like the answer. The instruction about 1 Across is part of the puzzle's gimmick, not the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to make fun of them in a friendly way, which is just what teasing is.

clue.text: Support in the library to reserve hotel in person

parts.note: to book is to reserve

indicators.note: the hotel letter goes inside the word for person

parts.note: self means one's person, one's own being
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Booking a hotel in person, set in a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelves hold up the volumes in a library, so a bookshelf is literally a support for them.

clue.text: One revered before the first year of Our Lord, I'm thinking, in the Colosseum?

definitions.note: the question mark flags an example of the answer

indicators.note: the saint comes ahead of the year in the answer

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is one who is revered

parts.words: the first year of Our Lord
parts.note: AD (anno Domini, in the year of Our Lord) with I, the Roman numeral one
UM is the sound of someone pausing to think

explanation.surface: Musing on a revered figure from the dawn of the Christian era in Rome's arena.
explanation.walkthrough: 'AD I' is year one of the Christian era. The Colosseum is the great ancient arena in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colosseum is an example of an arena for spectators, the sense of the answer here.

clue.text: Upright judge replaced by king in purge

indicators.note: the judge letter is swapped out and the king letter put in its place

parts.note: to eject is to expel, to purge
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An upright judge is replaced by a king in a political purge.
explanation.definitionFit: Erect means standing straight up, a synonym of upright.

clue.text: 25 Across, 5 Down turned up after following string along

indicators.note: the reversed letters come after the abbreviation

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the answer to 25 Across means without an end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the answer to 5 Down

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to two other answers turned around after some string.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 Down is LOOP; '25 Across' (ENDLESS) cuts its end to LOO, 'turned up' gives OOL, and F goes in front.
explanation.definitionFit: To string someone along is to deceive them, to make a fool of them.

clue.text: Annoyed as new water heater, failing to start, died

indicators.note: the first letter does not appear

parts.note: a kettle heats water
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A new water heater that would not start, then died, leaves someone annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nettled means irritated or riled, as if stung by a nettle.

clue.text: Dummy swallowed plant with bad smell

definitions.note: a dummy pill that is swallowed

parts.note: to plant something is to place it
BO is body odour, a bad smell

explanation.surface: A dummy swallowing a plant that smells bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowed' looks like a containment signal, but it belongs with 'Dummy': there is no insertion here.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a pill with no active drug, a dummy tablet that the patient swallows.

clue.text: See God's city for, unfortunately, the lowest of the low

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of the four preceding words are put in a new order

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit God's city, which turns sour for the poorest.
explanation.definitionFit: The dregs of society are the most despised people, the very lowest social class.

clue.text: Original day of 1 Across to 6 Across others

definitions.text: day of 1 Across to 6 Across others
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the ... of April, April Fools' Day, the day for teasing others

explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is the puzzle's unclued entry; read as April with 6 Across as TEASE, the day is the first of April, when people play tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Something original is the earliest of its kind; April Fools' Day falls on the opening date of that month.

clue.text: Broadcasting acceptable song

parts.note: ON means acceptable, as in 'that's not on'
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: A song suitable for broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted live over radio or television.

clue.text: Catholic state supported by us in Paris, like Notre Dame

indicators.note: in a down clue the French word sits below and holds up the rest

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
NOUS is French for us

explanation.surface: A Catholic state backed by the French, with the Paris cathedral as backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre Dame is a huge Gothic cathedral with a vast, hollow interior, so it is cavernous.

clue.text: Top Cambridge mathematician abandoning arithmetic, perhaps at the first opportunity, for calculator?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a pun: a calculating person, not a machine

indicators.note: the mathematician gives up a letter, which is left out
it is the first R that is dropped, not the later one

parts.note: at Cambridge University a wrangler is a student gaining first-class honours in mathematics
arithmetic is one of the three Rs, so R

explanation.surface: A top mathematician gives up arithmetic for a calculator.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic. 'Calculator' looks like the gadget but means a scheming, calculating person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wangler gets things by scheming and contrivance, so is a calculating, artful type.

clue.text: Cloth we fabricated using traditional methods

indicators.note: fabricated means made up or put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Cloth woven by hand the old-fashioned way.
explanation.definitionFit: Something low-tech relies on simple, older techniques rather than advanced technology.

clue.text: Starts to notice habitual halitosis, having, in elemental form, gas

parts.words: Starts to notice habitual halitosis, having, in elemental form
parts.note: the starts of notice, habitual, halitosis and having are N, H, H, H: in elemental form that is the chemical formula NH3

explanation.surface: Bad breath that is chronic and noticeable, smelling of some gas.
explanation.walkthrough: Written as chemical symbols, one nitrogen and three hydrogens is the formula of this pungent gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammonia is a colourless, sharp-smelling compound that is a gas at room temperature.

clue.text: 1 Across? I don't know …

definitions.meaning: first meaning: 1 Across has no clue printed, so it is literally lacking one
second meaning: a colloquial admission of total ignorance

explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across is the grid's unclued entry, so it is literally without a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no idea is the slang sense; the unclued entry is the literal sense of lacking a hint.

clue.text: Container prone to leaking — ridiculously wet, total bother

indicators.note: the letters behave absurdly, landing in a new order

explanation.surface: A leaky container causes a wet mess and much bother.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber bottle filled with hot water to warm a bed, notorious for springing leaks.

clue.text: Command and control

explanation.walkthrough: The two words look like a pair of near-synonyms joined; each is a separate sense of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: An order is an instruction, and order is also a state of discipline kept in a classroom or society.

clue.text: Making a face, head away for trip

indicators.note: the first letter is sent off

parts.note: pouting is pushing out the lips, making a face

explanation.surface: Someone sulking as they head away on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: An outing is an excursion or day trip.

clue.text: Smile awkwardly, maybe losing heart

indicators.note: placed awkwardly, the remaining letters end up in another order
the central letter is removed

explanation.surface: An awkward smile, possibly from someone losing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: MAYBE without its middle letter is MABE, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam is to give a broad, radiant smile.

clue.text: See 5 Down

parts.note: this clue sends you to 5 Down, which sends you straight back here, round and round for ever

explanation.walkthrough: 25 Across says 'See 5 Down' and 5 Down says 'See 25': the cross-references never resolve, which is exactly what the answer describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A computing term for a sequence of instructions that repeats forever without terminating.

clue.text: Mock debut of Stallone, a terrible actor

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: a ham is an actor who overacts badly

explanation.surface: A dig at Sylvester Stallone's acting debut.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock and sham both mean fake or imitation, as adjectives.

clue.text: See e.g. gents pursuing sex and the Bible in retreat

indicators.note: chasing behind, so the lavatory word comes last
retreating means going backwards, so these letters run right to left

parts.note: IT is a coy word for sex or sex appeal
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
the gents is a men's lavatory, and can is slang for a lavatory

explanation.surface: A scandal: men chasing sex and scripture in a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb but is the Holy See, the Pope's seat of government; 'the gents' is British for the men's toilets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See, the Pope's jurisdiction, is administered from Vatican City, so the two names are used interchangeably.

clue.text: See 6 Across directions

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
going across a map runs between the compass points east and west, E and W

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to another clue, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See 6 Across' looks like a cross-reference to TEASE; instead 6 is a Roman numeral and 'Across' belongs with 'directions'.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to view something is to look at or observe it.

clue.text: Walk briskly, then run from Tea Party participant

parts.note: to march is to walk with brisk, regular steps
to hare is to run fast

explanation.surface: Someone walking fast, then running away from a tea party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tea Party is the Mad Hatter's in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland, not a political one.
explanation.definitionFit: The March Hare is one of the guests at the Mad Hatter's tea party in Lewis Carroll's story.

clue.text: Island occasionally banned nature study in central location

indicators.note: every third letter of the word is banned, a regular occasional removal
only the letter at the centre of the word is used

parts.note: middle letter U

explanation.surface: An island where nature study is now banned, sometimes in a central spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the 3rd and 6th letters of NATURE (T, E) to get NAUR, then add U from the centre of STUDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a tiny island nation in the central Pacific, the world's smallest republic.
